serv.summary: The proposal description is insufficient to verify consistency with executable actions. While six token transfers are defined (3 USDC transfers and 3 UP token transfers to three addresses), the proposal text lacks recipient addresses, specific amounts, and clear mapping between named individuals and executable actions.

dolphin.summary: The proposal executes six token transfers but provides no on-chain binding between recipient addresses and named payees, and no amount reconciliation, creating substitution and mispayment risk.
findings: Action #1: The 400 USDC transfer to 0xCA7632327567796e51920F6b16373e92c7823854 is not cryptographically tied to David or any named payee in the proposal text; a compromised or substituted address would silently redirect funds, and Action #2 compounds this with 50,000 UP to the same address.

Action #3: The 700 USDC and 50,000 UP transfers to 0x38B826a4426A0D4d9b4377AC57C9Af0308281c5D lack any payee/amount mapping in the description, so reviewers cannot detect a malicious address swap or duplicate payment before execution.

Action #5: The 200 USDC and 150,000 UP transfers to 0x9dED35Aef86F3c826Ff8fe9240f9e7a9Fb2094e5 are materially different in UP amount from the other recipients and are unexplained; if UP is treasury-held governance value, this could be an unnoticed treasury drain rather than a routine payment.
